item.title: Baker Boy Takes Album, Song and Film Clip of the Year at 2026 NIMAs
item.description:
Here's a short, engaging podcast script based on the article:
[Intro music plays]
Host: "Welcome to our podcast, where we bring you the latest news and updates from the music world. Today, we're coming to you from the Darwin Amphitheater, where the 2026 National Indigenous Music Awards just took place. And what a night it was! Our top story: Baker Boy dominated the awards, taking home three of the night's top prizes."
[Short music transition]
Host: "Baker Boy, the Yolŋu rapper, won Album of the Year for his latest release, DJANDJAY. His single 'THICK SKIN', featuring Thelma Plum, Emma Donovan, Kee'ahn, and Jada Weazel, claimed both Song of the Year and Film Clip of the Year. And if that wasn't enough, he performed the track live at the ceremony, bringing out Emma Donovan as a surprise guest."
[Short music transition]
Host: "But Baker Boy wasn't the only winner of the night. Cousin duo Birdz and Fred Leone took home Artist of the Year, while Drifting Clouds won Best New Talent. We also saw Northern Peninsula Area win Community Clip of the Year for 'All The Way From The NPA', and Bulman School & Community earning the Indigenous Language Award for 'LOK LOK MAH BURARR'."
[Short music transition]
Host: "And in a special tribute, blues musician Marlene Cummins and Elcho Island's Saltwater Band were inducted into the NIMAs Hall of Fame. As MusicNT's Mark Smith said, 'Last night's celebration brought together some of the most incredible music and musicians this country produces, showcasing the rich connection of family and culture.'"
[Outro music plays]
Host: "That's all for today's episode. Congratulations to all the winners, and thank you for tuning in. We'll be back with more music news and updates soon."
